title: Barnabas
lead: Barnabas, a Levite from Cyprus whose given name was Joseph, was an early member of the Jerusalem church who sold a field and gave the money to the apostles (Acts 4:36-37). He brought the newly converted Saul to the apostles (Acts 9:27), fetched him from Tarsus to Antioch (Acts 11:25-26), and travelled with him on the first mission. Paul names him in Galatians as a partner at the Jerusalem meeting and as one who was carried away at Antioch (Galatians 2:1, 9, 13).

sections.b: Acts says that Paul and Barnabas split over John Mark after the Jerusalem meeting (Acts 15:36-40). Galatians 2:13 shows another strain: Barnabas, who had stood with Paul at Jerusalem, drew back from table fellowship with Gentiles at Antioch. Paul later speaks of him as a fellow worker who, like Paul, worked for his living (1 Corinthians 9:6). The Epistle of Barnabas is an early Christian writing that bears his name but is not by him, according to nearly all scholars.
